blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof ka sawal hai aur ek kabhi khatam na hone wala product hai. Ghabrane ki baat nahi: saare bases (2, 4, 8, 16) 2 ki powers hain.
Same base wali powers multiply hon to powers jama hoti hain, is liye poora product \(2^S\) ban jayega jahan \(S\) powers ka jama hai.
Aur mazay ki baat: yeh \(S\) khud ek infinite A.G.P. hai, jo hum abhi seekh chuke hain.
Plan: bases ko 2 ki powers mein likho, \(2^S\) banao, \(S\) nikalo, phir \(2^S\) hisaab karo. Left side se shuru kar ke right side (4) tak pohanchna hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2^{\frac12} \cdot 4^{\frac14} \cdot 8^{\frac18} \cdot 16^{\frac{1}{16}} \cdots\)
Humein find karna hai: saabit karna hai ke product 4 hai.
Tareeqa: Indices ke qawaneen \((x^m)^k = x^{mk}\) aur \(x^m x^k = x^{m+k}\), phir powers ke jama ke liye A.G.P. wala tareeqa.

Har base ko 2 ki power banayein
\[4 = 2^{2},\ 8 = 2^{3},\ 16 = 2^{4}\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2^{\frac12} (2^{2})^{\frac14}\]
\[\quad \times (2^{3})^{\frac18} (2^{4})^{\frac{1}{16}} \cdots\]
Kyun: Jab tak bases alag hain, powers jama nahi ho saktein. 4, 8, 16 ko 2 ki powers mein likhne se sab ka base 2 ho gaya.

Ek hi power mein jama karein
\[= 2^{\frac12} \cdot 2^{\frac24} \cdot 2^{\frac38} \cdot 2^{\frac{4}{16}} \cdots\]
\[= 2^{\frac12 + \frac24 + \frac38 + \frac{4}{16} + \cdots}\]
\[= 2^{S}\]
Kyun: Power ki power multiply hoti hai: \((2^2)^{\frac14} = 2^{2 \times \frac14} = 2^{\frac24}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac24\) ko abhi \(\frac12\) mat banayein, warna pattern (upar 1, 2, 3, 4) chhup jayega. Same base ki powers multiply hon to powers jama hoti hain, is liye poora product \(2^S\) hai.

Powers ka sum (infinite A.G.P.)
\[S = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{2}{4} + \dfrac{3}{8} + \dfrac{4}{16} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{8} + \dfrac{3}{16} + \cdots\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}S = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{8} + \cdots\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{1 - \frac{1}{2}} = 1\]
\[S = 2\]
Kyun: Powers \(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{4}, \frac{3}{8}, \ldots\) ke upar \(1, 2, 3, \ldots\) (A.P.) aur neeche \(2, 4, 8, \ldots\) (G.P., \(r = \frac12\)) hain. Yani yeh khud ek infinite A.G.P. hai! \(\frac12\) se multiply, shift aur minus: har jore se upar sirf 1 bachta hai, jaise \(\frac{2 - 1}{4} = \frac14\). Jo bacha woh infinite G.P. hai: pehla term \(\frac12\), ratio \(\frac12\), sum \(\frac{1/2}{1/2} = 1\). Is liye \(\frac12 S = 1\) aur \(S = 2\).

Product hisaab karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2^{S} = 2^{2} = 4 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: \(S = 2\) rakha to \(2^2 = 4\), jo bilkul right side hai. Saabit ho gaya.
